### New

**Color themes: schematic and PCB**
- **Settings → Color Themes and Fonts…** (or the 🎨 button in the Viewers group) opens a new dialog: pick a theme, copy it and edit its colors, with a live preview.
- Themes use **KiCad's color theme file** format. KiCad themes (`.json`) can be imported as they are, and exported files open in KiCad too.
- **The PCB viewer has themes too:** layer, background, board and hole colors come from the theme. Layers without a matching theme entry keep their original color.
- **18 new built-in themes from the KiCad community:** Catppuccin (4 flavors), Dracula, Tokyo Night, Gruvbox, Gruvbox Light, Witch Hazel, Monokai High Contrast, Skyline and more. 28 schematic and 18 PCB themes in total. Sources and licenses are under the **Licenses…** button in the dialog.
- **Sheet symbols stand out:** the fill of sheet symbols (blocks) is separate from the symbol body fill and can be edited; in every built-in theme blocks have a color distinct from the background and the symbols.
- All themes are embedded in the generated HTML. The theme selected in the dialog is the one the HTML opens with; the toolbar selector switches it in the browser.

**Fonts**
- Fonts can be chosen for schematic text, PCB labels (pad number, net name, measurement) and the viewer interface. The default is **Segoe UI**.
- The schematic font can also be changed from the toolbar in the browser; selection and clicking stay aligned.

### Behavior change
- In the built-in schematic themes the fill of sheet symbols changed: it is no longer the same as the symbol body.
- Viewers now open in Segoe UI by default. Choose **"Original font"** in the dialog for the previous look.

### Known limitations
- Font files are not embedded in the HTML: if the computer opening it lacks the selected font, the original font is used.
- PCB silkscreen text is artwork drawn by Altium, so it is not affected by the font setting.
- The 3D view is not affected by color themes.
